title: Sam Morgan choosing songs and playing the slapstick
summary: Sam picked the songs and used a hinged slapstick to keep time; Brown describes how it was built and says only Sam used it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Anything else about those records that you can remember? Who picked out the numbers or who wanted to, they played some of those spirituals, you know, like sing all of them.
Sam would pick all the songs out.

Well tell me, did he use the slapstick much? Oh yeah. I know he did on the dance job, I never heard the band in person. Did he use the slapstick on those records? I can't hear it much on the record, I don't think. Maybe it's there, I don't know.
Yeah, well he used, the slapstick was used then. He used the more? He used that slapstick everything he played.
When he would take down the trumpet, then he'd get the stick used.
He liked to play that stick.

Yes, he liked to play that thing. And well that would be most, him keeping his time, you know, with the music. That stick would make you hit right when he, you come out of, I guess, I don't know what he did it for, but I guess it was keeping time.
Yeah, it helped me a whole lot. And I guess it helped a whole lot of fellas a whole lot.
Did anybody else play the slapstick in that band? No, Sam the Only Man.
Is there any other band used to use a slapstick like that? I don't think.
Did he carry that around in his trumpet case or how did he carry that around? Do you remember how big a thing it was?

No, it was something about that long. About 14 inches. And it was bed supper like that, you see. On a hinge. Had hinge on this back then, you see. And it was a handle out this way and there were two flaps. You just play it with one hand? Yeah, one hand. Just like that.
